availability_note: Route 133 is the next sail lane west of Route 132 on the same Pacifidlog-Slateport trip; same gate<=68 pool-84 party as E0434/E0435 (Incineroar 36, Urshifu-S 42, Amoonguss 42, Landorus 42 legend, Tapu Fini 60 legend, Flutter Mane 68). Nothing from Underwater/Seafloor maps.

strategy_checks.check: Kingdra opens with Rain Dance or Muddy Water
strategy_checks.evidence: T1 Kingdra Mega Evolved and chose Rain Dance (denied by Fake Out flinch); T2 at 31/241 it chose Muddy Water instead of re-trying Rain Dance, which is the right call at that HP.
T1-T2 Hydro Pump into Incineroar (2x, 159 then KO); T4 Tailwind once Arctozolt was the incoming reserve.

strategy_checks.check: Rain + Tailwind stacking / Swift Swim speed tier
strategy_checks.evidence: Rain never went up: Fake Out flinched the T1 Rain Dance and Kingdra died on T2. The stack could not be tested in this line; that is the crack line working, not a defect.

strategy_checks.check: Arctozolt Bolt Beak used when it moves first
strategy_checks.evidence: T5 under Tailwind Arctozolt chose Bolt Beak into Tapu Fini (2x) and moved before it; Fini had Protected.

strategy_checks.check: Araquanid Water Bubble damage / Wide Guard vs spread
strategy_checks.evidence: T3 Liquidation OHKOed Flutter Mane (213/213). No spread move was aimed at it so Wide Guard was never relevant.

strategy_checks.check: Sticky Web only if it beats an immediate attack
strategy_checks.evidence: Araquanid attacked both turns it was on the field; never spent a turn on Sticky Web while under pressure.

protect_ledger.payoff: REAL - blocked Flutter Mane's Thunderbolt (2x, lethal on a 234-HP Lumineon) while Araquanid KOed Flutter Mane. Best possible use of the move.

protect_ledger.entry: Kingdra, Lumineon (other turns) and Arctozolt carry Protect and did not use it; no empty Protects.

engine_notes.note: Battle text printed 'The opposing Araquanid couldn't fully protect itself' when Urshifu's Wicked Blow hit an Araquanid that had chosen Liquidation, not a protect move. Cosmetic Unseen Fist message fires without a protect being active. Not an AI issue.

cooler: This is a good regular-trainer fight: two player faints, one genuinely well-timed Protect, and Bolt Beak forced a Protect read. The Mega Kingdra at offset 0 (L82) is the soft spot - it never got the rain up and fell to Wicked Blow twice - but a Fake Out lead is exactly the counterplay the crack describes. If anything (not this pass) the rain would be more robust from a Damp Rock on Lumineon's Tailwind partner or a second setter; species are fine.
authored_set_legality: No problem; all four sets played as written and Kingdra Mega Evolved on turn 1.
